title: Bring back parking minimums
summary: Requires parking with each new home again, as before January 2026; builders choose how much to add above it.

how: Planning staff draft the change to the Land Use Management Ordinance.
The Planning Commission reviews the proposal and makes a recommendation.
Residents comment at a Town Council public hearing.
Town Council votes on the change.

evidence.claim: Chapel Hill eliminated mandatory parking minimums across town on January 21, 2026
evidence.source: Town of Chapel Hill, Town Council adopts LUMO amendments (2026)

evidence.claim: After Buffalo dropped minimums, 47% of major projects built less parking than the old rules required
evidence.source: Hess & Rehler (2021), Journal of the American Planning Association

evidence.claim: A structured space costs ~$29,900 to build (2024 national median)
evidence.source: WGI Parking Structure Cost Outlook for 2024

pros: Every new building brings its own parking, so fewer new residents look for spaces on nearby streets.
cons: Builders pay for spaces they would not otherwise build, up to about $30,000 a space in garages.
Changes little where builders would build that much parking anyway.
